title: Microscope Slides in Motion — source and archive registry supplement 11

records.collection: Sir John Murray's H.M.S. Challenger sediment collection and microscopic preparations
records.type: expedition sediment collection + microscopic slides + historical registration + open dataset
records.date_scope: 1873–1876 collection; post-cruise study and later museum custody
records.holdings: The NHM preserves bottles, tubes, boxes, slides and derived preparations from H.M.S. Challenger. The current public dataset exposes collecting and preparation data from dredges, trawls, soundings, anchor mud and shallower-water collections. Haeckel's 1887 primary report says John Murray made carmine-stained Canada-balsam Radiolaria preparations on the spot and that Haeckel examined about one thousand preparations from 168 stations. A recent collection study describes a separate 105-drawer slide cabinet and records preparations annotated or made by specialists including Haeckel, Norman and Voigt & Hochgesang.
records.research_use: A rare end-to-end station-address system: expedition station, method/depth/locality, shipboard preparation, specialist study/publication, Murray/Edinburgh custody, British Museum/NHM registration, slide-cabinet address and current dataset record can potentially be crosswalked. It is also an authoritative reference against which claimed Challenger material in external museum or auction collections can be tested.
records.access: The collection dataset is openly downloadable through the NHM Data Portal; physical research and slide-cabinet access through NHM palaeontology/micropalaeontology collections.

records.collection: CT scans and modern reassessment of H.M.S. Challenger sediments
records.type: digital analytical afterlife + non-destructive imaging dataset
records.holdings: The NHM Data Portal publishes CT data used to examine Challenger samples while preserving the historical material. A recent study of 21 samples labelled as tow-net at dredge, weights, or trawl found benthic foraminifera, fragments and detrital material in most, indicating that some contained resuspended seafloor sediment rather than exclusively surface material.
records.research_use: A strong afterlife case showing that a historical collection-method label is itself an evidential claim that can be re-evaluated. Modern imaging adds a new analytical address to nineteenth-century material without requiring destructive washing or wet sieving, while the old station and collection labels remain available for comparison.
records.access: Open dataset and station-linked scan resources through the NHM Data Portal; individual files are large.
